source: docs/research/repo-intelligence.md (fourth research wave: 23 full four-angle harvests + 40 issue-tracker sweeps); corrected per docs/research/audit-2026-11-05/REPORT.md

candidates.candidate: Request-path retry and fallback ladder: classified transient-vs-terminal errors, Retry-After honored, per-provider cooldowns, and one whole-request deadline spanning all attempts
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy forwards each request exactly once (only discovery has transient retry, crates/llm-proxy-provider/src/discovery.rs:145, verified 2026-11-04). Every gateway in the wave treats classified retry/fallback as core, and the #1 cross-repo pain is misclassification that bans healthy capacity (sub2api #8442, CLIProxyAPI #7197, metapi #582).
candidates.crate: llm-proxy-server + llm-proxy-core + llm-proxy-storage (provider crate only for error classification; audit G)

candidates.candidate: Pre-answer in-band failover: stage the upstream stream (bounded buffer) until the first output event so an HTTP 200 followed by an SSE error frame can still be retried or failed over before any byte is committed
candidates.rationale: An OpenAI-compatible upstream can return 200 and then reject the stream in its first frame. Correction (audit): the chat upstream's {"error":..} frame was skipped as malformed before any recovery logic could help — leading frames produced a 502, later ones were masked as success — so the provider decoder had to be fixed first (plan 01 now emits an in-band error event and marks the ledger row failed); Anthropic-path in-band errors do surface to the client. CLIProxyAPI holds handshake frames in a 48-frame/1MiB budget; sub2api stages 64KiB-to-temp-file; Switchyard holds a one-role prelude.
candidates.crate: llm-proxy-adapters (decoder fix first), then llm-proxy-server (audit G)

candidates.candidate: Cache-token usage fidelity: parse OpenAI prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (chat and Responses shapes) and Anthropic 5m/1h cache splits into the existing core cache fields; price cache reads/writes at their own rates
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's core usage carries cache_creation/cache_read (crates/llm-proxy-protocol/src/core.rs:683-685; cite corrected per audit — :639-641 is Cost). Correction (audit): the columns were not fed only from Anthropic dialects — DeepSeek-style prompt_cache_hit/miss fields also fed them, wrongly booking uncached input as cache creation and zeroing prompt_tokens; the rescope includes that mapping fix. A grep for prompt_tokens_details/cached_tokens over crates/ and apps/ returned nothing (verified 2026-11-04), so OpenAI-dialect cached tokens never reached the ledger or cost estimates. Twelve repos show this exact gap breaking cost dashboards, budgets, and client auto-compaction.

candidates.candidate: Context-window preflight: estimate input tokens with the existing offline counter, reject over-limit requests before egress with dialect-exact typed errors (OpenAI context_length_exceeded, Anthropic 'prompt is too long', Responses response.failed)
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy already surfaces context_length on /v1/models (crates/llm-proxy-server/src/routes/models.rs:35,142) and ships an offline token counter, but never preflight-checks, so agents get raw upstream 400s and waste spend on doomed calls. mistral.rs shipped exactly this 'for coding agents'; opencodex shows clients branch on the mapped code to decide compact-vs-retry. Priority challenge (audit): the inputs are weak — context_length is None for OpenAI/Anthropic discovery lists, and the offline counter ignores tools, tool_result and images — so rejection needs a margin or a provider count.

candidates.candidate: Client-disconnect usage settlement: settle the cancellation row (estimated usage where the provider reports none); propagation itself already exists
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): upstream cancellation propagation already worked in every streaming phase (drop guard; probe E6), and a row does exist from RequestReceived before the await — a disconnect before the first event left a dangling row, now settled by plan 01. What was actually missing is usage settlement: ClientCancelled carried no usage payload, so tokens delivered before cancellation never settle. done-hub decouples the upstream call from the client context so billing always completes; otari writes an estimated row for abandoned streams.

candidates.candidate: Per-key budgets and multi-window rate limits (RPM/TPM/RPD) wired to the SQLite usage ledger, with in-flight USD reservation for max-output estimates
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): this candidate's in-flight USD reservation contradicted the compendium's check-then-accrue blueprint (CO:709) and the gap analysis's no-reservation stance — one admission model had to be picked, not three; and the limiter lives in llm-proxy-server/middleware, not llm-proxy-core. Plan 05 resolved the contradiction with one reserve-then-settle Admission step (unestimatable cost goes to an explicit policy). llm-proxy rate-limits per identity - caller key id when authenticated, client IP otherwise - but had no token (TPM) windows, per-key spend caps, or per-key model scoping. Eight repos ship per-key spend caps or multi-window limits; mcp-gateway's enforcer proves the hot-path cost (<0.1ms) in micro-USD atomics.
candidates.crate: llm-proxy-engine + llm-proxy-store (server + storage per audit G; the old 'core' mapping was wrong)

candidates.candidate: Usage-estimation fallback: inject stream_options.include_usage on OpenAI streams, force Accept-Encoding: identity upstream, estimate tokens when usage is absent, and flag rows usage_estimated
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): no Accept-Encoding header is sent at all (no compression feature on the HTTP client), so forcing identity is moot and was dropped; and a provenance discriminator already exists (UsageProvenance), so the proposed usage_estimated flag is redundant — extend provenance instead. Real gap: when an upstream omits usage (streams without stream_options, callers leaving mid-stream), llm-proxy recorded a synthetic-zero row rather than an estimated, flagged one. plano injected exactly these knobs after finding gzipped bodies landing in usage_missing; aisix estimates via bundled tiktoken and tells the client so a caller never reads zero against an unreconcilable bill.
candidates.crate: llm-proxy-adapters + llm-proxy-server + llm-proxy-protocol (provenance enum; audit G)

candidates.candidate: Phase-shaped timeouts: connect / first-byte (TTFB) / in-stream idle / total, cross-validated at config load, replacing the single flat per-route timeout
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): there is no single flat timeout — four phases already exist (connect 10s, headers 60s hard-coded, per-chunk idle 60s, per-route TimeoutLayer to the response head); they simply were not operator-configurable and lacked a total stream deadline. Rescope: make the phases configurable, cross-validate at load, add the total deadline. Seven repos shape timeouts around LLM stream phases; reasoning models that think for minutes before the first token are killed by flat budgets.

candidates.candidate: Client-facing /v1/responses endpoint: streaming event synthesis, wire-exact usage fields, and Codex-proven tool-call grouping/ordering semantics
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's client surface is OpenAI Chat + Anthropic Messages only. Eleven repos serve Responses to clients; one-hub users demand it because Codex-class clients cannot be pointed elsewhere, and its merged PR shows Responses SSE clients hard-require wire-exact usage fields (a zero-value cached_tokens omitted via omitempty broke Codex). completion-to-response is the minimal implementation shape.

candidates.candidate: Egress header hygiene: strip client auth/Origin/browser headers on the upstream hop, never re-attach credentials across redirects, and sanitize client-supplied request ids in logs
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): stripping client headers was moot — nothing was ever forwarded (the upstream request type carries no inbound headers); the real and urgent defect was the main client following redirects and sending x-api-key/x-goog-api-key plus the body cross-host (fixed in plan 01: same-origin only). The inverse gap was unlisted: no inbound header (e.g. anthropic-beta, session headers) ever reached upstream, so beta features could not be enabled per request — plan 02 added the per-provider forwarding allowlist. The cloudflare-workers fix shows caller auth headers overriding provider credentials; llama-swap shows browser Origin headers making Anthropic 401; freellmpool shows redirects leaking credentials to internal targets.
candidates.crate: llm-proxy-transport (redirect policy) + llm-proxy-server (forwarding allowlist; audit G — the old 'server' mapping for stripping was wrong)

candidates.candidate: Loopback hardening: validate Host/Origin (DNS-rebinding defense) in mode=none, and refuse non-loopback binds without client auth at config validation
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): refusing non-loopback binds without client auth already existed (config validation), and candidate #25 proposed the same refusal — the two overlapped. Kept scope: Host/Origin validation (DNS-rebinding defense) in mode=none, which was genuinely absent. mcp-gateway shipped an always-on Origin/Host guard as a CWE-346 fix after an external report that a web page could reach the loopback port; jan refused non-loopback binds without a key and stopped '*' trusted-hosts from accepting every Host.

candidates.candidate: Subscription OAuth upstream credentials: PKCE browser-login and device-code flows, single-flight proactive refresh, and quota-window telemetry surfaced to the client
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy accepts only static bearer keys upstream (SecretString in TOML). Seven repos make consumer-subscription upstreams (Codex/ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Kimi) first-class; claude-code-proxy proves the full flow fits a small Rust binary, and its PR #149 shows quota/reset clocks mapped into the Anthropic usage block. Correction (audit): rated 'high' with no mention of vendor terms — Anthropic and Google bar routing through consumer subscription credentials, which the original entry did not disclose.
candidates.dropped: Dropped per the credentials decision in docs/goal.md (audit question Q4): subscription OAuth and client fingerprinting are not built; vendor terms bar routing consumer credentials through third-party software. See docs/README.md 'Not planned'.

candidates.candidate: Reasoning-parameter translation: reasoning_effort <-> thinking.budget_tokens <-> Gemini thinkingBudget with per-model clamps, and enforcement of declared budgets
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy passes Thinking content blocks through but converts no reasoning parameters between dialects. CLIProxyAPI ships a dedicated conversion engine; Switchyard derives effort from budget ratios with loss diagnostics; bedrock-gateway shows per-generation thinking-API churn breaking static translation; mistral.rs shows accepted-but-unenforced budgets silently spending the whole window.
candidates.crate: llm-proxy-adapters (provider edge, per docs/protocol.md:166-168; audit G — the old 'protocol' mapping was wrong)

candidates.candidate: SSE keep-alive heartbeats during silent generation, plus a guaranteed terminal usage event on every stream including tool-call turns
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): heartbeats already exist after the first upstream event (3s SSE keep-alive comments) and the terminal usage chunk exists but carried zeros when upstream sent usage after finish (fixed in plan 01). Rescope: cover silence before the commit point (nothing was sent for the first ~4s and intermediaries time out) and guarantee real terminal usage on every stream including tool-call turns. done-hub ::PING and Switchyard's requested event: ping target the silent window; koboldcpp shows agent auto-compaction never firing when the terminal usage chunk is dropped on streamed tool requests.

candidates.candidate: Prompt-cache hygiene: normalize cache-busting volatile bytes (client correlation tokens, per-turn reminder blocks) before egress, keep any request mutation byte-stable past the last cache breakpoint, and optionally auto-inject cache markers
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy performs no request-body normalization, no cache_control/prompt_cache_key injection, and has no mutation-safety boundary. ostk-cache measured cache_read going 0 -> 963K tokens/turn just by stripping one volatile token; sub2api engineered fingerprint convergence for the same effect; plano injects markers per provider family.
candidates.crate: llm-proxy-adapters (provider edge, per docs/protocol.md:166-168; audit G — the old 'core' mapping was wrong)

candidates.candidate: Cross-protocol reasoning/tool-state replay: preserve Gemini thought signatures on replayed function calls, round-trip OpenAI reasoning_content (never omit when empty), and carry encrypted reasoning through signatures
candidates.rationale: metapi shows Gemini upstreams 400-ing replayed tool history missing thought_signature; done-hub ships the sentinel-retry recovery; completion-to-response shows omitting empty reasoning_content breaking DeepSeek multi-turn; claude-code-proxy packs encrypted reasoning into a synthetic signature the client echoes back.

candidates.candidate: Session attribution and optional sticky affinity: record session/conversation ids (from client headers like x-claude-code-session-id and metadata.user_id) on usage rows; optionally pin a session to an upstream for cache locality
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's ledger records only the key id; nine repos attribute per-session and several pin sessions to upstreams explicitly for prompt-cache warmth. otari users cannot see their own spend without session grouping; CCR's fallback misattribution shows why the served model must be recorded per row.

candidates.candidate: Per-key model/provider allowlists (glob patterns) enforced after authentication
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): the premise was overstated — the catalog allow/deny check runs only when catalog.enforce=true (default false), so keys reached beyond the catalog by default, not 'everything the catalog exposes'. Four repos ship per-key scoping; CLIProxyAPI's PR shows restricted keys must fail closed for requests without an identifiable model.

candidates.candidate: Gemini-native client ingress: POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent and :streamGenerateContent translated through the existing hub (Gemini is currently upstream-only)
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy speaks only OpenAI Chat and Anthropic Messages on the client side. Seven harvested repos serve native Gemini clients - ThinkWatch routes them through the identical pipeline (limits, routing, guards, billing), done-hub mounts a sibling /v1beta group sharing the /v1 middleware chain, and antirion accepts Gemini and Bedrock client dialects inbound. This clears the record's 3+ recurring-needs threshold, unlike the two-repo Ollama dialect candidate that follows it.

candidates.candidate: Upstream health and quota-state tracking: passive parsing of 429/rate-limit headers into per-provider cooldowns keyed to real reset times, plus a synthetic probe that auto-disables unreachable models
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's only upstream health notion is discovery-time transient retry. yolorouter parses exactly three dialects and derives bench duration from learned rows with a corroboration cap; sub2api pauses accounts by real quota windows; metapi auto-disables models past probe thresholds; xlb pairs active probes with passive ejection.

candidates.candidate: Prometheus exposition and OTel export of the existing lock-free metrics
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's metrics are in-process counters with no scrape or export path. Five repos treat OTel/Prometheus as a standard subsystem; redis-vl's contributor note says 'every deployment writes its own counters' when a library exports none.

candidates.candidate: Pricing catalog sync from models.dev (with refresh and aliasing) plus an explicit unpriced state that is never silently $0
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): row-level unpriced was already distinct — cost stays NULL against a 0 'unmetered' price and the row API returns an Option; only the usage summary folded unpriced rows to 0. The real gaps are no refresh story for the operator-typed fixed-point TOML and the summary fold. Six repos converge on models.dev as the canonical feed; RouterArena charges unpriced models the table maximum instead of $0 after silent skips corrupted evaluations; tokdiet shows an unpriced month looking like a free month.

candidates.candidate: Hot config reload with refusal semantics: surgical per-provider swaps that never tear down unrelated connections, with restart-required refusals instead of half-applied changes
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy requires a restart for config changes. Five repos ship hot reload; mcphub's worst production pain was config edits re-spawning every upstream; mcp-gateway refuses auth-weakening reloads with stable error prefixes and a restart_required flag; preflight keeps the previous runtime on a failed reload.

candidates.candidate: Idempotency-key replay for retried POSTs: claim the key before budget checks, replay the stored response for matching retries, 409 while in flight
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): the dedup window was off by default and time-based from first sighting (not concurrent-only), caller-blind, and 409s a sequential repeat — stock SDKs retry 409, and it would have 409'd an idempotent replay ahead of any claim logic. The durable need stands: a client retry after a timeout re-executes and re-bills. mcp-gateway's admission holds active leases that never expire by design; otari's fingerprint covers request-shaping headers so old claims still match; xlb gates replay of non-idempotent requests on the key's presence.

candidates.candidate: Config-validation hardening: refuse cleartext credentials on http:// URLs to off-machine hosts; warn/refuse on non-loopback binds without auth
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): the non-loopback refusal half already existed at config validation, duplicating candidate #11; the kept scope is the cleartext-credential check. llm-proxy only validated that an endpoint scheme is http or https, so an api_key over plain http to a remote host was accepted silently. mcp-gateway refuses credential-bearing cleartext configs before startup, loopback exempt with an explicit opt-in.
candidates.crate: llm-proxy-core (bind clause dropped as duplicate of #11; audit G)

candidates.candidate: `doctor` command: live provider reachability checks, per-model one-token verification probes, and named remedies for failures
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's `validate` is static config validation and `status` is liveness. mcp-gateway's doctor runs live checks into a pass/fail/warn table where every failure carries fix/verify/rollback commands; the awesome-ai-gateway ecosystem ships standalone key-liveness monitors because balance pages stay green while keys are dead.

candidates.candidate: In-flight request visibility: expose live requests (provider, model, state, elapsed) in the admin API alongside completed usage rows
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): the admin API did not report only completed usage — /usage/requests has no completed_at filter and rows are written from RequestReceived, so in-flight rows already return with completed_at null. The real gap: in-flight rows are indistinguishable from dangling ones and carry no state or elapsed time. Routerly's users asked explicitly for live views; claude-code-proxy and ollamaMQ ship them as first-class operator surfaces.

candidates.candidate: Streaming truncation semantics: never synthesize success on an abnormal end; emit typed in-band error events carrying finish-reason context
candidates.rationale: Correction (audit): the premise was backwards — llm-proxy itself masked truncation as success (a cut-off stream ended end_turn with a ResponseCompleted row, and a test required that synthetic terminal), and leading errors returned 200 in-band rather than being deferred. Raised to high: keep the valid wire framing but mark the failure. The ecosystem failure it points at is real (sub2api #8505, koboldcpp #2481, jan #9515, CCR #1917). Typed terminal events let clients decide retry-safety.

candidates.candidate: Streaming tool-call fragment robustness: longest-match tool-name resolution and tolerance for quotes/newlines inside JSON arguments during fragment reassembly
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's SSE decoders keep tool-arg fragment state; the recurring upstream failure mode in the wild is ambiguous tool-name prefixes (search vs search_web silently executing the wrong tool) and quotes/newlines inside streamed JSON arguments.
candidates.dropped: Dropped per audit: no fragment reassembly exists to harden — the SSE decoders pass tool-argument deltas through unparsed and keep only index maps, so neither failure mode (longest-match tool names, quote tolerance in reassembly) applies. See docs/README.md 'Not planned'.

candidates.candidate: Per-provider concurrency caps with bounded admission: semaphore-limited in-flight requests per provider/model, returning 503 (not 429) with a short Retry-After when saturated
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy has no concurrency cap anywhere in the egress path. xlb's RAII lease and queue_full 503, metapi's per-site max_concurrency, and ollamaMQ's per-model caps all exist because capacity shedding misread as rate-limiting arms hour-long client backoff ladders (llama-swap #1256).

candidates.candidate: Provider API-key pools: multiple credentials per provider with rotation, cooldown on 401/429/5xx, and utilization-aware ordering
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy supports one static key per provider. Users of one-hub forks call the one-key-per-channel shape 'very inconvenient' (done-hub #57); CCR's users file it as the top missing feature (#1923); the cloudflare-workers discovery path already rotates on 429 within a request.

candidates.candidate: Self-loop prevention: refuse configurations whose upstream resolves to the proxy's own listener, and stamp/strip a hop header on egress
candidates.rationale: These proxies are configured via base-URL swaps, where a wrong URL silently creates infinite forwarding. ostk-cache refuses self-referential upstreams and 508s on hop-header ingress; inference-gateway short-circuits calls that loop back through its own listener.

candidates.candidate: Retention hygiene: prove ledger retention knobs drive eviction, and never orphan sidecar data when pruning
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's SQLite ledger has max_age/max_rows/prune_interval; the ecosystem shows retention bugs where body files outlive rows (13 GB of orphans in nine days on CCR) and capacity knobs that never reach the backend (llama-cpp-python disk cache).
candidates.dropped: Dropped per audit: retention knobs are real and already proven by tests, and no sidecar data exists to orphan. See docs/README.md 'Not planned'.

candidates.candidate: Config provenance: print resolved settings with the source of each (CLI > env > config > default)
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy supports three override layers (config, env interpolation, CLI) but `validate` prints resolved values without origins, leaving 'why is my flag ignored?' unanswerable. ostk-cache's Source-tagged --print-config answers it from output.

candidates.candidate: Admin/ops MCP surface: expose the admin usage API as MCP tools so an agent can operate the proxy itself
candidates.rationale: Three gateways expose their management plane over MCP (inference-gateway stateless 2026-07-28; done-hub's per-user dashboard tool; sub2api's four pre-configured read/write servers reusing REST ownership checks). llm-proxy's read-only admin API is the natural substrate.

candidates.candidate: Ollama-native client dialect (/api/chat, /api/generate, /api/tags) reusing the existing admission chain
candidates.rationale: llm-proxy's inbound surface is OpenAI Chat + Anthropic Messages only. ollamaMQ serves the full Ollama surface on both sides; opencodex added an Ollama-compatible inbound API by reusing one admission path rather than new code - the low-cost pattern for dialect breadth. Kept at low priority despite sitting below the record's 3+ repo threshold (unlike the Gemini ingress candidate above): local-inference alignment is strategic for llm-proxy but the harvested demand is two repos.

candidates.candidate: Cache-Control: no-store on all admin API responses
candidates.rationale: done-hub shipped this after a CDN cached authenticated API responses into an authorization bypass. Correction (audit): llm-proxy did not 'emit no Cache-Control/Pragma headers anywhere' — the SSE route already sets no-cache; the admin API responses carried none, and that is the gap.

candidates.candidate: Retry terminality signals: when llm-proxy exhausts its own retries, mark the final error non-retryable (x-should-retry: false plus a computed Retry-After) so client retry loops don't stack
candidates.rationale: Sequenced after the retry ladder (#1), which it depends on: with no retries in the proxy, there was no exhaustion to signal (audit). claude-code-proxy's exhausted 503 lacked x-should-retry:false, so Claude Code stacked its own retry loop on the proxy's - one deterministic turn hung ~30 minutes over ~100 upstream calls. ThinkWatch returns computed Retry-After plus x-should-retry: false on every refusal.

candidates.candidate: Fix the 30-second server exit: the shutdown deadline started at startup, so the default config force-exited the server (status 1) 30 s after launch with no signal, dropping in-flight work and skipping ledger close
candidates.rationale: Audit bug row 1 / BUG-1 (critical): serve_with_deadline started the graceful-shutdown deadline at startup; shutdown_timeout="0s" only avoided it. Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Stop deleting blocks that carry a cache_control ttl: a 1h marker made the whole system or text block unrepresentable on the wire and it was silently deleted from the prompt with HTTP 200
candidates.rationale: Audit bug row 2 / BUG-2 (high): the strict wire decoder deleted the containing block (warn only), so the system prompt or user text vanished. Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Request-field fidelity: the OpenAI client path dropped 11 of 17 tested fields (response_format, parallel_tool_calls, seed, n, logprobs, logit_bias, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, service_tier, prompt_cache_key, store) with HTTP 200, and the Anthropic path 400'd on stop_sequences, top_k, service_tier, output_config and cache_control on tools/server tools
candidates.rationale: Audit bug rows 8-9 / BUG-18, BUG-19: docs/protocol.md:158-164 requires a warning or rejection when omission changes behavior; both were violated. Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Message-level cache markers: only system-prompt markers survived the Anthropic-to-Anthropic path; message text and tool_result markers were dropped, so conversation caching could not work through the proxy
candidates.rationale: Audit bug rows 10-11 / BUG-5: decoded into the core, then dropped at the upstream adapter; the core had no cache field on ToolResult. Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Anthropic stream usage and stop reason: the documented message_delta usage shape (output_tokens only) failed to parse and message_start usage was ignored, so clients and the ledger got 0/0 usage and max_tokens became end_turn; cache tokens were lost
candidates.rationale: Audit bug row 4 / BUG-3 (high): a fixture locked the absence in. Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Inbound header allowlist: no inbound header (anthropic-beta, session headers) ever reached the upstream, so per-request beta features could not be enabled
candidates.rationale: Audit bug row 12: the upstream request type carried no inbound headers at all, which also made candidate #10's stripping proposal moot. Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Same-dialect passthrough: when client and provider speak the same format, keep the raw body and apply only the proxy's own edits, so unknown fields survive instead of being normalized away
candidates.rationale: Audit feature conflict 10: a fully normalized hub breaks both strict providers (Anthropic rejects unknown fields; OpenAI drops them). Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Contract tests from real client traffic: capture Claude Code, Codex, OpenAI SDK and Anthropic SDK traffic, strip secrets, and replay it against a fake upstream in CI
candidates.rationale: Audit 'Recommended order' step 2 and modularity review: the suite passed while every bug in the table existed, and one fixture locked a bug in. Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Client-key lookup that scales: a cache miss tried every configured key in sequence, so 1,000 keys meant ~1,000 argon2 runs per bad token
candidates.rationale: Audit feature conflict 12 (middleware.rs:475-490): use a key-id prefix plus one verification, or a keyed hash of high-entropy tokens. Missing from the backlog entirely.

candidates.candidate: Extract a request engine out of the HTTP layer: the pipeline was private, returned axum types, and 13 backlog candidates were mapped to llm-proxy-server where SDK users cannot reach them
candidates.rationale: Audit 'Modularity and SDK readiness': building the server-mapped candidates first would weld them to axum. Missing from the backlog entirely.

corrections_note: Corrections applied per the 2026-11-05 research audit ('Backlog review' and evidence section G): rationales restated where they were wrong, candidates #5/#8/#11/#14/#25/#27 rescoped to the real gap, #28 raised to high, #6 resolved to the one admission model built by plan 05, and crate mappings corrected. Every candidate now records 'plan': the completed plan (docs/completed/) that consumed it, or null plus a 'dropped' reason. Plan 03 restructured the workspace crates (llm-proxy-provider split into adapters + transport; llm-proxy-engine added), so 'crate' keeps the audit-corrected, pre-restructure name and 'plan' is the authoritative landing spot. The ten items the audit found missing from the backlog entirely are appended at the end.
